page.title: Rewards Catalog
page.purpose: Let the minter declare what tokens buy, with the availability and approval posture that make the economy theirs rather than the product's.

priorities.statement: Approval posture is chosen deliberately per entry, not inherited from a global default.
priorities.notes: This is the control that makes a small reward instant and a large one considered.

priorities.statement: Availability — a window, a quantity, or unlimited — is explicit.
The catalog is understood as the household's own vocabulary, not a list the product supplied.

states.description: No entries; the page invites the minter to describe what tokens should buy, with examples that are clearly examples.
An entry is being created or updated.
Entries loaded but per-entry redemption counts failed; entries render with that column marked unavailable.
Showing a cached catalog after a failed refresh, labelled as such so a retired entry is not trusted as live.

elements.name: Catalog entries
elements.description: Each entry with cost, availability and approval posture.

elements.name: Approval
elements.description: Settles immediately, or waits for approval.

claims.statement: Approval posture is a required, explicit choice on every entry with no silent default.
Availability is stated on every entry rather than implied by absence.
Example rewards in the empty state are visibly examples and are not created by accident.
